scope: Source candidate audit of all 23 work packages and 116 acceptance requirements. Full testing is deferred at owner request.
meaning: Source traceability and implementation intent only. References and a covered row are not evidence that runtime behavior passed. No acceptance result was changed.
sourceFindingsResolved: Configured Happier/Hermes state homes were missing from checkpoints.
Direct Codex relay could compete with Happier daemon without coexistence qualification.
Claude autostart had an unguarded duplicate editor launcher.
Web-kiosk/GUI lifecycle, resource limits and managed browser checkpoints were incomplete.
Plan-only VM input and acceptance prose retained obsolete installer/native/desktop assumptions.
Raw Nix Hermes public-origin validation diverged from guided validation.

baseline.behavior: The exported 244-file baseline and provenance are recorded; source changes preserve the original tree rather than replacing it.
baseline.remaining: A release must bind its own source/lock; this audit is not a published release.

identity.behavior: Canonical Ed25519 keys are bounded, structurally parsed, noninteractively checked as a complete set before provisioning side effects; damaged persistent identity is refused.
identity.remaining: Real disk, permission and VM fault qualification is deferred.

storage.behavior: Sparse home and disposable-root behavior, exact private disk modes, create-only metadata, seed permissions and QEMU read/write error stops are retained.
storage.remaining: Native ISO, actual sparse allocation and QEMU fault qualification remains unrun.

ssh-worker.behavior: Dedicated controller/health OpenSSH configuration and accumulated-setting checks protect the managed worker alias; ordinary owner SSH configuration is not universally audited.
ssh-worker.remaining: Real client channels and Desktop helper invocation require route-specific evidence.

presets.behavior: Four purposes and 13 data presets resolve once to frozen ordinary settings, explicit exclusions, dependencies and placement; eight-agent suggestions do not become runtime subscriptions.
presets.remaining: Installation and later update behavior still require real system qualification.

selection.behavior: The shared purpose-first selection routine handles explicit dependency/authority consent, independent removals, nested Back, cancellation and per-app native status without authentication or activation.
selection.remaining: 29 scripted scenarios pass; the real PTY/installer/system fixture is deferred.

configure.behavior: Configure previews a bounded settings diff, evaluates effective overrides, preserves local.nix and worker resources, builds/admit before publication and refuses routine persistent topology conversion.
configure.remaining: Build/activation failure injection and real local override qualification are deferred.

installer.behavior: Prepared storage, disk identity, explicit pre-write authorization, release authentication, power/boot contracts and worker image admission remain authoritative around the new selection flow.
installer.remaining: No real installation, destructive disk action or hardware preflight was run.

catalog.behavior: Retired IDs fail actionably, raw selections stay opt-in, nano/tmux remain base, exact commands and independently removable component metadata are generated from one catalog.
catalog.remaining: Actual all-curated command resolution and closure builds remain unrun.

packages.behavior: Happier artifacts and Hermes/Pi/OMP recipes are independently held/pinned; Hermes optional voice/model dependencies are pruned, Grok aliases contained and managed vendor installers/updaters guarded.
packages.remaining: Both architectures, old CPU instructions, helper identity and offline activation need actual build/runtime evidence.

native-package.behavior: Selected native clients use guarded public commands/desktop entries and guarded autostart; normal portal/keyring prerequisites are independent of Code/Cowork qualification.
native-package.remaining: No native/account enforcement contract ships qualified; opaque/client-managed helpers need exact-build review.

egress.behavior: Standalone execution-UID IPv4/IPv6 rules run after destination translation, allow inbound reply direction, deny private/local brokers by default, scope DNS/receiving-socket IPC and revoke execution when rules stop.
egress.remaining: Real IPv6/NAT/overlay, namespaces, DNS/proxies, receiver cgroups, reload and failure behavior is deferred; no internet-exfiltration or hostile-root claim.

tailscale.behavior: Guided Tailscale support is optional and unenrolled; authority stays root-only, route acceptance/Tailscale SSH are off, and deselection omits the Serve backend package and timer.
tailscale.remaining: Real enrollment/grants/overlay access is an owner qualification step; simulated tailscale0 is not an authenticated overlay pass.

serve.behavior: Only explicit selected dashboard paths are reconciled against a durable root-owned ownership journal; retirement withdraws owned routes before stopping a backend and preserves foreign mappings.
serve.remaining: Real Serve enrollment, HTTPS/native auth, forged headers, revocation and ownership recovery require owner-run evidence.

lifecycle.behavior: Nix declares one foreground provider supervisor with runtime/config/permission-bound setup markers, private bounded diagnostics, durable disable, bounded backoff and permanent-refusal stops.
lifecycle.remaining: Harmless substitute programs do not qualify actual provider auth, daemon behavior, task recovery or paid inference.

happier.behavior: The declared start-sync supervisor, scoped home/relay/E2EE environment and exact selected agent executable paths are checked against the pinned upstream dry-run/path oracle; URL auth is the integrated setup route.
happier.remaining: Real E2EE, auth/scope, adapters, expiry/revocation, approval/cancel/resume and pairing effects remain unrun. SSH pair-remote is a trusted-client procedure requiring side-effect qualification, not an enabled Assbox onboarding path; Pi/OMP built-in adapters are not asserted.

openclaw.behavior: OpenClaw keeps its upstream gateway/onboard/node interfaces, loopback UI and private dashboard profile; agent/plugin authority and selected dependencies stay in the execution domain.
openclaw.remaining: Channel allowlists, selected ACP/plugin provisioning, tool policy and actual delegation must be established with upstream configuration and authenticated tasks; no universal Assbox adapter is invented.

hermes.behavior: Hermes CLI/gateway/dashboard share the pinned family, explicit persistent service home and lazy-install deny; dashboard uses loopback binding plus an exact non-loopback HTTPS origin or separately consented tunnel-only profile.
hermes.remaining: Gateway allowlists, dashboard fail-closed auth, cookies/origins/WebSocket/PTY and upstream delegation need exact-release authenticated tests. URL syntax is not an auth pass.

native-routes.behavior: Claude relay, Cursor worker, OpenClaw node, OpenCode and VS Code tunnel keep distinct lifecycles, consent and credentials; Antigravity/direct Codex require reviewed immutable foreground argv or remain staged.
native-routes.remaining: Provider-specific client/auth/runtime tests remain unrun. Direct relay stays experimental and active coexistence with Happier is rejected; ordinary SSH launches no Assbox Codex daemon.

opencode.behavior: OpenCode uses a private execution-owned credential loader for its loopback server and explicit frontend; private exposure is separately selected.
opencode.remaining: Authenticated remote browser behavior and actual exposure require qualification.

native-policy.behavior: Immutable exact client/platform/account contracts, complete independent surface inventories, bounded root probes and boot/monotonic freshness authorize a supervised native client; absence/conflict/staleness keeps only the affected app inactive.
native-policy.remaining: Native probes must actually establish all selected account/helper/policy surfaces. Synthetic receipts cannot qualify enforcement, safe login, Work/cloud transitions, no fallback, preview/plugins or Linux mobile hosting.

cowork.behavior: Cloud task authority is an explicit native feature; eligible local Cowork requires its own exact provider-VM contract, current entitlement/isolation probe and conditional helper closure without automatic device groups.
cowork.remaining: Post-6-October rollout/topology is observed per account/build; local device/share/storage/resource qualification is conditional and unrun. No pre-transition migration or Code-SSH equivalence is asserted.

presentation.behavior: X11/Openbox and optional Wayland retain portals, keyring and autologin/session recovery; explicit protected native Code selects a worker, not controller-local arbitrary execution.
presentation.remaining: Real native windows, keyring lock/reboot, GUI coexistence, crash and physical device qualification are deferred.

web-kiosk.behavior: Explicit web kiosks have separate protected browser profiles/policies, durable Chromium service control, resource limits and checkpoint quiescence; they are not implicit native fallbacks.
web-kiosk.remaining: Real browser policy and native-product feature equivalence is not claimed; graphical provider login and network behavior require their own tests.

computer-use.behavior: Opt-in resources omit desktop closure by default, scrub physical state, serialize leases, manage private Xauthority/D-Bus and provide ephemeral sandboxed Chromium with loopback debugging under bounded user scopes.
computer-use.remaining: The substrate VM is wired but unrun. Cursor provider-managed and Hermes/OMP existing-display tool paths, cleanup and collision behavior need exact-provider tests. Optional viewing remains an upstream private authenticated feature requiring separate qualification; no viewer or broad listener is provisioned by default.

resources.behavior: Managed native, provider, web-kiosk and autostart GUI services account and bound memory/CPU; manual computer-use scopes and background Nix/zram policy have separate limits.
resources.remaining: Pressure/peak memory, old CPU, provider VM and real hardware behavior are unmeasured; limits are not reservations or guaranteed minimums.

state.behavior: Root-private bounded checkpoints quiesce declared services, include configured Happier/Hermes homes and managed browser profiles; explicit local restore checks identity/integrity and leaves a recovery journal and execution stopped.
state.remaining: Provider DB migration, restore, rollback and power-loss tests remain unrun. Direct sessions need owner quiescence; links and custom editor/project paths need explicit export/selection; no cross-instance credential migration.

maintenance.behavior: Existing authenticated staging, journal recovery, boot receipt compatibility, bounded scheduling/retry/power/grace and conservative retention are preserved; liveness is local and non-billable.
maintenance.remaining: No provider recovery/replay semantics or database rollback is inferred from OS lifecycle; actual outage and pressure tests remain deferred.

release.behavior: New held families participate in graph composition, both-architecture checks, immutable source/lock authentication and existing numeric publication authority; coverage/security/system gates are retained.
release.remaining: No release promotion/publication was performed. Build/security gates and owner-authenticated feature results are distinct; no unrun feature is promoted to qualified.

documentation.behavior: One product contract, generated catalog/preset tables, scoped operational examples and separate execution/credential/graphical authority guides replace contradictory global assumptions.
documentation.remaining: Provider facts stay dated and external owner responsibilities remain explicit; source documents do not attest to actual deployments.

evidence.behavior: Dated Linux computer-use rows distinguish native product/harness/auth/build scope and upstream evidence from exact Assbox result; Mac, mobile-through-Mac, Linux worker and experimental relay remain separate.
evidence.remaining: All 116 release requirements remain not_run with null evidence. Evidence updates never change resolver rules or installed selection.

external-coder.behavior: Minimal external Desktop SSH presets select standalone guest tools/workload SSH, exact login-shell runtime and deliberate access; macOS/hypervisor sharing and availability remain owner responsibilities.
external-coder.remaining: Real Mac/Desktop app-server lifetime/channels, guest auth/egress, host sharing, matching CPU, Claude helper and both Tailscale variants remain unrun. Generic SSH tests are not a Desktop pass.

external-fixture.behavior: Source-bound owner-run host/guest canaries and non-idempotent counters detect selected-path fallback/replay across initial/disconnected/reconnected tasks without automating Desktop or network control.
external-fixture.remaining: Temporary-directory self-checks pass; actual native route/mobile/handoff tests remain unrun. The fixture explicitly reports routeQualification not_established even when its observed canary sequence passes.

qualification.behavior: The complete work/acceptance ledgers and wired release/native/system fixtures preserve the full testing handoff; commands and scoped lightweight results are recorded independently.
qualification.remaining: Full W21/W22 static/system/security/auth/hardware execution is deferred at owner request; unavailable prerequisites and conditional applicability need explicit future records.

requirements.title: Sparse storage and QEMU error behavior
External SSH identity and channel policy
External client outage and explicit handoff

limitations: No Nix package/system/image build, VM, native/provider login, real network, disk or hardware test ran during this audit.
Exact native account/helper enforcement and conditional provider-VM contracts are absent until qualified; affected clients stay inactive.
Antigravity and direct Codex service argv remain staged by default, pending supported pinned foreground contracts.
Provider CUA, optional authenticated viewing, ACP/plugin configuration and SSH pairing side effects require upstream-specific qualification; generic resources or a CLI install cannot supply it.
Release promotion is separate from these source commits and remains subject to the existing full gates.
